_comment: 🔮️ Basic FM Handover's own contribution to the repository test platform: `ruststep` 0.4 registered as the independent ISO 10303-21 reader for this subset's `Ifc2x3CobieMutation` vocabulary, and the mutation catalog it is measured against. The vocabulary is NOT the ✳️any subset's -- ✳️any declares generic Part-21 graph editing and knows nothing about model view definitions, while every kind below is one COBie handover sheet, taken from the conformance gate this repository already implements in production (`../🧬️schema/🦀️component.rs`'s `check_cobie_conformance`). The `semantic-ifc-v1` comparison profile is the ✳️any subset's own contribution, reused rather than copied.

oracles.rationale: IFC2X3 is physically ISO 10303-21 syntax under the IFC2X3 EXPRESS schema, and `ruststep` 0.4 parses it exactly as it parses STEP AP214 -- already linked and already registered for the sibling `ifc 2x3/✳️any` and `step ap214/✳️any` subsets, re-confirmed here against this subset's own real input (the committed 3464-entity slice of a real 21 MB IFC2X3 EDM export). It has NO writer at all, which per the fleet brief's §6 rules out `@mode-differential`: it cannot be a second PRODUCER of mutated bytes. It is registered strictly as the INDEPENDENT READER -- every mutation this subset's dispatcher performs (ruststep parse plus the standard-level from-scratch Part-21 writer at `../../../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs`, never this repository's own production `step::engine::part21` writer) is read back through a FRESH `ruststep::ast::Exchange::from_str` call before `semantic-ifc-v1` compares it. STRONGER REFERENCE EVALUATED AND NOT ADOPTED: `ifcopenshell` 0.8.4 (Python) is the canonical IFC toolkit, reads AND writes IFC, and would make a genuine `@mode-differential` possible for these MVD subsets; it installed and imported successfully in this environment and the repository's Python oracle host has landed (precedent: `🗿️artifacts/📄️pdf/🧪️tests/extract-text-pdf-1-4/🐍️component.py` with `pypdf`). It was NOT adopted because putting a Python distribution on a generated host's import path requires an `oracleHostPackages` entry in the SHARED `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🧪️oracle/🔣️component.json` (host packages resolve by owner prefix, and a subset manifest is not a prefix of the case owner `🗿️artifacts/🏗️ifc`), and this wave's brief forbids an executor from editing the shared stdio manifest. A governance boundary, not a capability gap.
